title: Alterac Mountains
body: These cold peaks between Lordaeron and the Hillsbrad foothills were once the human kingdom of Alterac, which began as a city-state of old Arathor. The kingdom died with its king's treason in the Second War and never recovered. Ogres now hold its ruined capital and outlaw nobles its villages, the ruins of Dalaran lie on the shore of Lordamere Lake, and somewhere in the eastern hills the assassins of Ravenholdt keep their hidden manor.

title: Strahnbrad
body: Strahnbrad was a mountain village of Lordaeron. In the Third War Blackrock orcs raided it for slaves to sacrifice, and Prince Arthas and Uther rode to its defense, but many of its people died all the same and the rest are long gone. Today it is the Syndicate's main base, and among its outlaws walk the shadow mages of the Argus Wake, on business of their own.

title: Ruins of Alterac
body: The capital of Alterac emptied when the kingdom fell, and after the Third War the Crushridge ogres moved into its deserted halls. Their warlord rules from the old palace now. Somewhere in the rubble, rumor says, an ogre mage called Grel'borg dug up the Perenolde Tiara, an heirloom of the royal family made by Ironforge jewelers and set with emeralds.

title: Dalaran Crater
body: On the shore of Lordamere Lake lie the ruins of Dalaran, the city of the Kirin Tor, laid waste in the Third War. Broken walls ring its outskirts, where summoners and their bound elementals stand guard over the rubble, and a few archmages keep watch over what is left.

parts.body: Over the heart of the city the survivors have raised a great violet dome that no outsider can pass. Behind it, it is said, the Kirin Tor are rebuilding.
In time the Kirin Tor finished their work and lifted the city whole into the skies of Northrend. All that remains on the lakeshore is a crater beneath a dome faded nearly to nothing.

title: Ravenholdt Manor
body: Hidden in the hills above Hillsbrad, at the end of a winding mountain path, stands Ravenholdt Manor, seat of the Assassin's League. Strangers are warned to watch their backs. Within, the League keeps everything its trade needs: a poison seller, an engineer, quiet gardens, and a training arena that is the domain of the orc Master Kang.

title: Lord Aliden Perenolde
body: Aliden is the eldest son of Aiden Perenolde, the king who sold out the Alliance. For two years after the Second War he served under Aedelas Blackmoore at Durnholde, trying to wash the stain from his name. Then he left for the mountains, founded the Syndicate, and now styles himself lord of Alterac from a manor at Dandred's Fold.

parts.body: He means to make slaves of the orcs who stand against him, as his father and Blackmoore once planned, and his mistress Elysa wears the pendant the Warchief sent his orcs to recover.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Aliden_Perenolde (eldest son of Aiden; two years clearing the name; Durnholde under Blackmoore; left to run operations in Alterac)

parts.body: He dies in his own manor at Dandred's Fold, among the outlaws he gathered to win back his father's kingdom.

title: Mug'thol
body: Mug'thol is warlord of the Crushridge ogres and master of ruined Alterac. The Banshee Queen once bound him to her will and sent him into Alterac after a relic, the Crown of Will; he put the crown on, and it set him free. The Forsaken have not forgiven him, and Southshore fears his ogres will come down from the mountains next.

parts.body: He falls amid the ruins of the old palace he made his seat, and the Crushridge are left without their master.

title: Nagaz
body: Nagaz keeps close beside Lord Aliden Perenolde at Dandred's Fold, though what he is to the outlaw nobles is not plain to see. Strange company walks the Syndicate's camps besides him: the shadow mages of the Argus Wake, who come and go on business of their own.

parts.body: His decoded letter shows what he is: the Argus Wake's hierophant in Alterac, signing in the name of Sargeras. He means to make the Syndicate rulers of Alterac again and turn them on Stromgarde, winning the Wake a nation from which to prepare for the Legion's Third Host.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Nagaz (positioned himself close to Perenolde)

parts.body: Nagaz dies at Dandred's Fold beside the lord he kept so close, yet his shadow mages still walk the Syndicate's camps.

title: Lord Jorach Ravenholdt
body: Lord Jorach Ravenholdt is master of the Assassin's League. He greets those he needs with open arms and rewards loyal service well, but keeps his own secrets close: what was in the sealed azure bag he once lost, he says, is a private matter. His grand master, Fahrad, trains the League's rogues and sends everyone else away.

title: Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver
body: Ansirem Runeweaver sat on the Council of Six that governed Dalaran in the Third War. When the Scourge came and Antonidas fell, he fought outside the walls against Arthas while Kel'Thuzad called down the demon lord Archimonde. He keeps watch now beside the ruins on the shore of Lordamere Lake.

parts.body: When Dalaran rose into the skies of Northrend, Ansirem was among the few mages who chose to stay behind at the crater it left on the lakeshore.

title: Archmage Cedric
body: Archmage Cedric is an agent of the Violet Eye, the order the Kirin Tor set long ago to watch over Karazhan and its master Medivh. He waits among the ruins of Dalaran, unmoved by the desolation and sure that the city is as powerful as ever, and reports from the Eye's agents in Deadwind Pass come to him.

parts.body: Karazhan sealed itself long ago, and the Eye's agents inside were never heard from again. Only Medivh or his apprentice Khadgar was thought able to open it, and Khadgar, long presumed dead, has been found alive in Shattrath.
